name: Duomo di Milano
description: Milan’s iconic Gothic cathedral, famous for its spires and the golden Madonnina statue on top.

name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
description: One of the oldest shopping galleries in the world, featuring 19th-century iron and glass architecture.

name: Teatro alla Scala
description: One of the most prestigious opera houses in the world, inaugurated in 1778.

name: Castello Sforzesco
description: A medieval fortress hosting several museums and masterpieces, including Michelangelo’s last sculpture.

name: Parco Sempione
description: Large public park behind Castello Sforzesco, ideal for walks and relaxation.

name: Santa Maria delle Grazie
description: Church housing Leonardo da Vinci’s Last Supper, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Navigli District
description: Historic canal district known for its vibrant nightlife, bars, and restaurants.

name: Pinacoteca di Brera
description: One of Italy’s most important art galleries, featuring Renaissance masterpieces.

name: Arco della Pace
description: A neoclassical triumphal arch located at the northern entrance of Parco Sempione.

name: Basilica di Sant'Ambrogio
description: One of the oldest churches in Milan and a prime example of Lombard Romanesque architecture.

name: Quadrilatero della Moda
description: Milan’s luxury fashion district, home to some of the world’s most exclusive boutiques.

name: Mercato Centrale Milano
description: Modern food market offering a wide selection of Italian cuisine and local products.

name: Torre Branca
description: Panoramic tower in Parco Sempione offering 360-degree views over Milan.

name: Colonne di San Lorenzo
description: Ancient Roman columns dating back to the 2nd century, now a popular social gathering spot.

name: Pirelli Hangar Bicocca
description: Contemporary art space located in a former industrial building.

name: Luini Panzerotti
description: Famous takeaway spot known for its freshly baked panzerotti.

name: Eataly Smeraldo
description: Large Italian food market combining restaurants, shops, and culinary experiences.

name: Pasticceria Marchesi
description: Historic pastry shop offering refined Italian desserts and coffee.

name: Bosco Verticale
description: Innovative residential towers covered with trees and plants, symbol of modern Milan.

name: CityLife District
description: Modern urban district featuring contemporary architecture, parks, and shopping areas.

name: Fondazione Prada
description: Contemporary art and cultural center designed by architect Rem Koolhaas.

name: Cimitero Monumentale
description: Monumental cemetery known for its impressive tombs and artistic sculptures.

name: Porta Nuova Skyline
description: Modern skyline area showcasing Milan’s contemporary architecture.

name: Università degli Studi di Milano
description: Historic university complex located in a former Renaissance hospital.
